key_concepts: Earth's axis is tilted at 23.5 degrees
Northern and Southern Hemispheres receive different amounts of direct sunlight
In June, the Northern Hemisphere receives more direct rays and experiences summer
In December, the Southern Hemisphere receives more direct rays while the Northern Hemisphe
Direct rays strike the ground at 90 degrees
Higher sun angles concentrate solar energy on a smaller area, causing more heating
Lower sun angles spread solar energy over a wider area, causing cooler temperatures
Seasons result from Earth's tilt and the shifting direct rays as Earth orbits the Sun
Temperate zones between 23.5 degrees and 66.5 degrees latitude experience four seasons
Tropical regions like the Philippines have rainy and dry seasons, not winter
The Sun appears to rise in the east and set in the west
